data:
The build is driven by hatchling and a small custom build hook at scripts/hatch_build.py, which compiles Hugo with the Go toolchain and places the binary inside the wheel. Building the deploy edition of Hugo (the withdeploy build tag) from source requires the following dependencies:
The Git version control system Python ≥ 3.10 The Hugo binary is pure Go and is compiled with CGO_ENABLED=0, so no C or C++ compiler is needed on any platform, including for cross-compilation.
hatchling and go-bin (the Go compiler toolchain) are pulled in as build-time dependencies automatically by the build backend, so you do not need to install them yourself. On 32-bit ARM Linux, where go-bin has no wheels, the official Go toolchain is downloaded directly instead. This is what makes the piwheels builds work.
Clone the repository and install the package:
Linux/macOSWindows git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/agriyakhetarpal/hugo-python-distributions cd hugo-python-distributions python -m venv venv source venv/bin/activate pip install . git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/agriyakhetarpal/hugo-python-distributions cd hugo-python-distributions py -m venv venv venv\Scripts\activate.bat pip install . For an editable install:
pip install -e . The Go build and module caches are kept in a temporary directory and removed after each build. To reuse them across builds, point the HUGO_BUILD_CACHE environment variable at a directory of your choice.
data.build-the-wheel#Build the wheel:
python -m build --wheel -Cgoos=linux -Cgoarch=arm64 Setting GOOS and GOARCH in the environment works as well, if you have a tool that does not work with config settings. If only one of the two is given, the other defaults to the platform of the running interpreter.
Some examples are showcased below.
Linux arm64Windows arm64macOS arm64 to macOS x86_64 python -m build --wheel -Cgoos=linux -Cgoarch=arm64 # builds into dist/hugo--py3-none-linux_aarch64.whl python -m build --wheel -Cgoos=windows -Cgoarch=arm64 # builds into dist/hugo--py3-none-win_arm64.whl python -m build --wheel -Cgoos=darwin -Cgoarch=amd64 # builds into dist/hugo--py3-none-macosx__x86_64.whl The macOS deployment target in the tag comes from the MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET environment variable if set. Otherwise, it comes from the running macOS version.
data.cross-compiling-for-different-architectu:
Since the binary is purely in Go, the Go toolchain handles cross-compilation on its own. No cross-compiler toolchains are involved. The target is selected with the goos and goarch config settings, which an in-tree build backend wrapper at scripts/hugo_build_backend.py translates into the GOOS and GOARCH environment variables for the Go build. The build hook then tags the wheel for the target platform, both across platforms and across architectures on the same platform.
Cross-compilation for Hugo binaries is provided for the following platforms and architectures, based on GOOS/GOARCH combinations that the Go toolchain supports:
macOS: darwin/arm64 and darwin/amd64 Linux: linux/amd64, linux/arm64, linux/arm, linux/386, linux/ppc64le, linux/s390x, and linux/riscv64 Windows: windows/amd64, windows/arm64, and windows/386 For a list of supported distributions for Go, please run the go tool dist list command on your system.

data:
A subset of the platforms supported by Hugo itself are supported by these wheels for hugo via hugo-python-distributions. The plan is to support as many platforms as possible with Python wheels and platform tags. Please refer to the following table for a list of supported platforms and architectures:
Platform Architecture Support macOS x86_64 (Intel) ✅ macOS 13.0 (Ventura) and later macOS arm64 (Silicon) ✅ macOS 13.0 (Ventura) and later Linux amd64 ✅ glibc 2.17 and later Linux arm64 ✅ glibc 2.17 and later Linux s390x ✅ glibc 2.17 and later Linux ppc64le ✅ glibc 2.17 and later Linux armv6l ✅ via piwheels 1 Linux armv7l ✅ via piwheels 1 Windows x86_64 ✅ Windows arm64 ✅ Windows x86 ✅ 2 DragonFlyBSD amd64 ❌ Will not receive support3 FreeBSD amd64 ❌ Will not receive support3 OpenBSD amd64 ❌ Will not receive support3 NetBSD amd64 ❌ Will not receive support3 Solaris amd64 ❌ Will not receive support3 For instructions on building Hugo for a specific platform or architecture, including cross-compilation, see Building from sources.
Wheels for Raspberry Pi (ARMv6l and ARMv7l) are built and distributed by piwheels, a community service that provides pre-compiled Python wheels for Raspberry Pi devices. These are not published to PyPI and are only available via the piwheels index. To install, add --extra-index-url https://www.piwheels.org/simple to your pip install command, or configure it permanently in your pip.conf. Raspberry Pi OS includes this index by default. ↩︎ ↩︎
The 32-bit (i686) wheels for Windows are cross-compiled with the Go toolchain from 64-bit runners, and the resulting binaries are tested in CI through the WoW64 compatibility layer. This target is not officially supported by the Hugo project, which does not publish 32-bit Windows binaries. Please refer to the Building from source section for more information on how to build Hugo for other platforms and architectures locally. If you need official support for a platform or face any bugs, please consider contacting the Hugo authors by opening an issue. ↩︎
Support for these platforms is not possible to include because of i. the lack of resources to test and build for them and ii. the lack of support for these platform specifications in Python packaging standards and tooling. If you need support for these platforms, please consider downloading the official Hugo binaries for these platforms. ↩︎ ↩︎ ↩︎ ↩︎ ↩︎
